messages:
jessica-support: Hey team — customer (acct 123456789012) flagged AWS Marketplace invoice showing ~2.4M Inference Token Units for 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-07, but our Redwood usage dashboard shows ~1.2M. They pasted a snippet of the marketplace CSV they received.

jessica-support: ```
line_item_id,sku,usage_quantity,usage_start,usage_end,order_id
LI-0001,mkt-infer-01,1200000,2026-03-01,2026-03-07,695-abc
LI-0002,mkt-infer-01,1200000,2026-03-01,2026-03-07,695-abc
```

sam-billing: Thanks — can you confirm the customer's marketplace account id and whether they have any reseller mappings? Also please upload the full CSV to the portal. Quick idea: could be duplicate metering events or two different dimensions mapped to same internal unit.

amy-cs: Customer confirms single AWS account (123456789012) and no reseller. They've uploaded the full CSV to the support portal.

billing-bot: Auto-mapped CSV uploaded by jessica-support: /uploads/1923456789/customer1234_marketplace.csv (parsed 42 rows)

michael-eng: Running a join between marketplace_records and usage_events to see how rows map. Query I'm running:

michael-eng: ```sql
SELECT mr.metering_id, mr.usage_quantity, ue.token_count, mr.order_id
FROM marketplace_records mr
LEFT JOIN usage_events ue ON mr.external_event_id = ue.external_id
WHERE mr.order_id = '695-abc'
```

michael-eng: Preliminary result: there are two marketplace_records for the same order where one of them has an external_event_id that matches our usage_events and the other has the same external_event_id but was written by an older exporter path that didn't populate all join keys -> the left join shows one null and one matched. In short: duplicate rows referencing the same external event.

sam-billing: That would explain the 2x. Marketplace billed both rows. We need to dedupe the exported records and submit an adjustment/credit request to AWS. Can you prepare a backfill to remove duplicate marketplace_records for the order?

michael-eng: Yes. Root cause appears to be a legacy connector emitting both a daily_aggregate and a tenant_aggregate row for identical events during a feature-flag rollout. Proposed fix: enforce uniqueness on (external_event_id, order_id) in the metering-export job and add an idempotency key.

michael-eng: Repro steps I ran locally:
- checkout release/connector-fix
- run metering-export for sample order -> produced two rows (daily + tenant)
- apply dedupe patch -> single row emitted

michael-eng: Backfill SQL we used to remove duplicates for that order (applied to records >= 2026-03-01):

michael-eng: ```sql
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY external_event_id, order_id ORDER BY created_at) rn
  FROM marketplace_records
  WHERE order_id = '695-abc' AND created_at >= '2026-03-01'
)
DELETE FROM marketplace_records WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM ranked WHERE rn > 1);
```

sam-billing: Patch pushed to staging and backfill executed against production-copy. After backfill, we should submit a usage adjustment report to AWS so they can reconcile the duplicated consumption. I'll open the AWS support case and request a credit for the duplicated 1.2M token quantity.

billing-bot: Ticket created: AWS-CASE-2026-000123 (https://aws.amazon.com/support/cases/2026-000123)

jessica-support: Customer asked for ETA on credit and assurance this won't reoccur.

michael-eng: Timeline: dedupe fix merged and scheduled deploy to prod tomorrow 03:00 UTC. Backfill already ran for the affected date range. Preventive measures: idempotency keys, export-level uniqueness, and a release validation that compares deduped export totals against internal totals before sending.

amy-cs: I'll update the customer now: explain the fix, that we've backfilled their data, opened the AWS case, and expect AWS response in ~48-72 hours.

sam-billing: Also adding a monitoring alert to billing dashboard that flags if marketplace CSV totals deviate >10% from internal deduped totals for the same order_id/date_range.

michael-eng: Postmortem action items: add feature-flag rollback checklist, add integration test that simulates connector emitting duplicate aggregate types, and run daily reconciliation between marketplace_records and usage_events.

jessica-support: Closing loop with customer — will follow up when AWS confirms credit. :thumbsup:

amy-cs: Customer replied: "Thanks, appreciate the quick fix and the follow up" :white_check_mark:
